issues.evidence: The Guides have the perfection of wisdom as their domain (their range of activity), not a home.
issues.fix: Perfect wisdom is the place where they move and work, like a beautiful garden.

issues.span: the river of craving and strong wanting
issues.evidence: The text has only the river of craving (srid pa'i chu klung); 'strong wanting' is a gloss of the same word, not a second thing.
issues.fix: He dries up the river of craving, which is strong wanting.

issues.span: A king might not visit the towns and lands of his kingdom.
issues.evidence: The king does not go to the villages or provinces; it is a fact, not a possibility.
issues.fix: A king does not go to the towns and lands of his kingdom.

issues.span: Do not hold on to the heaps of awakening. Do not have any clinging to the supreme!
issues.evidence: One single instruction: do not cling to the supreme by being attached to the aggregates of awakening. Splitting it into two commands loses the 'by' link.
issues.fix: Do not cling to the supreme by holding on to the heaps of awakening!

issues.span: They are bright lamps who stay completely calm. They speak the highest teaching.
issues.evidence: 'Illuminators' is dropped, and 'imperturbable' belongs to the speakers of the supreme Dharma, not to the lamps.
issues.fix: They light up the way and are lamps. They speak the highest teaching and cannot be shaken.

issues.evidence: Ungrammatical use of the locked phrase; the Tibetan says they are irreversible.
issues.fix: They are ones who never turn back.

issues.evidence: 'Those of great renown'; 'heroes' is added and may be confused with 'awakening hero'.
issues.fix: These very famous ones put on armor for hard deeds.

issues.span: No one can just figure it out or reach it.
issues.evidence: No one realizes it, and there is no attaining of it. The children's text turns 'not realized/no attaining' into 'cannot easily figure out or reach', which changes the logic.
issues.fix: No one has realized it, and there is nothing to be reached.

issues.evidence: He felt little inclination (to teach), thinking no one would understand.
issues.fix: he felt little wish to teach
